Nyirtass Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírtass, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews settled in Nyírtass around 1750 as peddlers under the protection of the Eszterházy family, and the congregation formally organized in the early 19th century. The cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1854, and it remained active until at least 1943. The community grew from 150 residents in 1840 to a peak of 325 in 1920, building its first synagogue and a well-regarded yeshiva by 1910. Nyírtass holds particular significance in Hasidic history as the birthplace of the Tosh dynasty: Rabbi Elimelech Segal Lowi, its second Rebbe, perished in Auschwitz in 1944 after Hungarian authorities forced the community to the Kisvárda Ghetto during Passover that year. Only a handful of survivors returned after the war to find their homes taken over and the mikvah and synagogue demolished; most soon emigrated to Canada, founding 'Kiryas Tosh' in Boisbriand, Quebec - still home to Tosher Hasidim today.
